headline: AI Pauses, Proof and Perimeter
thesis: Districts in New York and Los Angeles pause classroom AI while higher ed asks where AI truly adds value — and security teams warn AI is speeding up attackers.
summary: This week's coverage centers on accountability for AI in education. EdSurge reports on NYC and LA pausing classroom AI and asks what proof of safety and efficacy should look like; Inside Higher Ed notes Educause's 2027 Top 10 now leads with determining where AI adds real value, and a Maryland trial found only ~15% of students used an AI study assistant. THE Journal flags shadow AI, AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and ransomware aimed at staff families. Ed-Fi's state data stories and the November 9–11 Summit, plus 1EdTech's November webinars, keep interoperability in view.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · OCTOBER 29, 2026 · Search-snippet based; ETI, EdTech Week and EdTech Digest had no items dated this week, and EdTech Magazine and ISTE showed no October news.

themes.title: AI Pauses & Proof
themes.body: NYC and LA pauses raise the question of what evidence shows a tool is safe and effective; teens often reach banned tools anyway.

themes.title: AI Value & Evidence
themes.body: Educause ranks where AI adds real value first, a Maryland trial saw ~15% uptake, and KPMG finds only 12% consistently weigh AI value against cost.

themes.title: Security & Shadow AI
themes.body: Shadow AI, faster vulnerability discovery and ransomware targeting staff families raise the stakes for school and campus IT.

themes.title: People, Jobs & Skills
themes.body: Employers expect AI to make degrees more important, universities are hiring AI philosophers, and ISTE cohorts build educator capacity.

themes.title: Data & Interoperability
themes.body: Ed-Fi state stories (SC, TX, MI, NE) and 1EdTech's Caliper, CASE and badges sessions show shared standards in practice.

themes.title: Civics, Sovereignty & Access
themes.body: AI and elections literacy, midterm civics lessons and calls for higher-ed tech sovereignty frame who controls tools and information.
